slides.title: Protocols and Duck Typing (PEP 544)
slides.prompt: `Protocol` provides static duck typing (structural subtyping). Classes do not need to explicitly inherit from a Protocol; as long as they implement the required methods/attributes, static type checkers accept them.

slides.title: Protocol Base Class Import
slides.prompt: Fill in the base class imported from typing to enable structural subtyping.

slides.title: Nominal vs Structural Subtyping
slides.prompt: What is the key difference between ABCs and Protocols in Python static analysis?
options: ABCs require explicit inheritance (nominal subtyping), while Protocols inspect methods/attributes matching (structural subtyping)
Protocols enforce checks at runtime while ABCs operate strictly at compile time
ABCs support multiple inheritance while Protocols do not
Protocols can only define class attributes, not methods
slides.correctAnswer: ABCs require explicit inheritance (nominal subtyping), while Protocols inspect methods/attributes matching (structural subtyping)

slides.prompt: Fill in the decorator applied to Protocols to enable `isinstance()` checks at runtime.

slides.title: Combining Protocols
slides.prompt: Fill in the syntax to create a protocol `ReadWritable` that combines `Readable` and `Writable` protocols.

slides.title: @runtime_checkable Behavior Limitation
slides.prompt: What is a known limitation of `@runtime_checkable` when performing `isinstance()` checks on Protocols at runtime?
options: It checks only for the existence of required methods/attributes, not their function parameter signatures or return types
It raises a TypeError if used on classes with custom __init__ constructors
It cannot be combined with dataclasses
It disables static analysis in Mypy
slides.correctAnswer: It checks only for the existence of required methods/attributes, not their function parameter signatures or return types
